nodes.name: NiCo-LDH Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Detailed synthetic procedure of NiCo-LDH microsphere precursor with Ni/Co ratio of 4:3 (see Supporting Information, Scheme S1, Fig. S1, Fig. S3). The phase purity confirmed by XRD and shows hierarchical microflower morphology with nanosheet formation due to preferred orientation of layered structure.
nodes.source_text: The hierarchical NiCoP microflower was prepared as shown in Scheme S1. The phase purity of NiCo-LDH is confirmed by the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern in Fig. S1 and NiCo-LDH shows the hierarchical microflower morphology in Fig. S3.

nodes.name: NiCoP Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: NiCo-LDH microspheres grown on Ni foam were subjected to phosphorization treatment at 300°C, converting to hierarchical NiCoP microflowers assembled from NiCoP nanosheets (~50 nm thickness). The nanosheet curvature results from hydroxide loss during annealing.

nodes.source_text: using NiCo-layered double hydroxide (NiCo-LDH) microsphere as precursor followed by phosphorization... annealing at 300°C. The SEM image in Fig. 1b suggests the hierarchical microflower morphology of NiCoP after phosphorization.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP shows diffraction peaks at 41.0°, 47.6° and 54.5° assigned to NiCoP (JCPDS No. 71-2336) with no impurities detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of the NiCoP, Co_xP, and Ni_2P in Fig. 1a show similar diffraction peaks at 41.0°, 47.6° and 54.5°, which can be assigned to those of NiCoP (JCPDS No. 71-2336), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP maintains hierarchical microflower morphology assembled by nanosheets with thickness ~50 nm after phosphorization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image in Fig. 1b suggests the hierarchical microflower morphology of NiCoP after phosphorization. High magnification SEM image in Fig. 1c shows NiCoP microsphere are assembled by NiCoP nanosheets and the thickness is ~50 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP microsphere diameter is about 3.5 μm with no obvious amorphous oxide shell observed on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) image in Fig. 1d reveals that the diameter of the microsphere is about 3.5 μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP shows lattice fringes with spacings of 0.22 nm and 0.20 nm assigning to (111) and (201) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image shown in Fig. 1e and f reveals the lattice fringes with spacings of 0.22 and 0.20 nm, assigning to the (111) and (201) planes of NiCoP, consistent with our XRD analysis, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Co, and P elements are uniformly distributed in NiCoP microsphere with oxygen from surface oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental image of NiCoP in Fig. 1g confirms the uniformly distribution of Ni, Co, and P elements in the NiCoP microsphere body.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP shows BET surface area of 52.48 m²/g, higher than Co_xP (49.93 m²/g) and Ni2P (38.08 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S4 displays the N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms and the NiCoP shows the largest Brunauer Emmett Teller (BET) surface area of 52.48 m² g⁻¹, which is higher than those of Co_xP (49.93 m² g⁻¹) and Ni_2P (38.08 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP shows Ni 2p peaks at 852.8/870.2 eV (Ni^δ+) and 856.6/874.3 eV (oxidized Ni-POx/Ni^2+); Co 2p peaks at 777.9/793.4 eV (Co^δ+) and 781.8/797.9 eV (oxidized Co-POx/Co^2+); P 2p peaks at 129.4 eV (P^δ-) and 133.8 eV (P-O); O 1s peaks at 531.1 eV (MOx) and 532.4 eV (P-O); Ni:Co ratio close to 4:3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum in Fig. S5a is deconvoluted and shows two major doublet peaks at 852.8/870.2 and 856.6/874.3 eV... The doublet peaks located at 852.8/870.2 eV represent the Ni species (Ni^δ+) while those at 856.6/874.3 eV to the oxidized Ni-POx (Ni^2+). Similarly, in the Co 2p core level spectrum (Fig. S5b), the doublet peak located at 777.9/793.4 eV corresponds to the Co species (Co^δ+) for Co-P bonds... The P 2p spectrum shows two visible peaks at 129.4 and 133.8 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: After HER, NiCoP shows thin amorphous shell on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex-situ HRTEM images of NiCoP after the long-term reaction in Fig. 2d. A thin and amorphous shell is observed on the surface of the NiCoP catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: After HER, NiCoP Ni 2p shows major peak at 855.6/873.0 eV assigned to Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectrum of Ni 2p only exhibits one major doublet peak at 855.6/873.0 eV assigned to the Ni(OH)₂ (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER, NiCoP shows obvious amorphous surface layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image of the electrode after OER test is shown in Fig. 3d and an obvious amorphous surface layer is captured on the surface of NiCoP electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER, NiCoP Ni 2p shows major peak at 855.6/873.0 eV attributed to Ni(Co)OOH species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To determine the surface layer of NiCoP, the ex-situ XPS spectra of NiCoP of Ni 2p spectrum is carried out in Fig. 3e. Similar to the HER result, one major doublet peak at 855.6/873.0 eV, which is attributed to Ni(Co)OOH species.

nodes.characterization_summary: During HER resting, NiCoP shows characteristic peaks at 494 cm⁻¹ and 536 cm⁻¹ for Ni(OH)₂ and Co(OH)₂ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectra reveal that the characteristic peaks at 494 and 536 cm⁻¹, which can be assigned to the formation of metal-oxygen vibrations for Ni(OH)₂ and Co(OH)₂, respectively, gradually increase.

nodes.characterization_summary: During OER at ~1.3 V, NiCoP shows peaks at 475 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending) and 555 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g} stretching) of Ni(Co)OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: During the CV scan towards higher voltage, the characteristic peaks at 475 and 555 cm⁻¹, which can be assigned to e_g bending vibration and the A_{1g} stretching vibration of Ni(Co)O in Ni(Co)OOH, start to appear at ~1.3 V and gradually increases afterwards.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP C_dl = 40.10 mF cm⁻² for HER, higher than Co_xP (9.15 mF cm⁻²) and Ni₂P (7.61 mF cm⁻²), indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl of NiCoP is 40.10 mF cm⁻², which is obviously higher than those of Co_xP (9.15 mF cm⁻²) and Ni_2P (7.61 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP shows smallest charge transfer resistance of 1.18 Ω for HER, compared to Co_xP (1.23 Ω) and Ni₂P (1.53 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) (Fig. S13) of NiCoP reveals the smallest charge transfer resistance (1.18 Ω), compared with those of Co_xP (1.23 Ω) and Ni₂P (1.53 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCoP C_dl = 4.25 mF cm⁻² for OER, higher than Co_xP (3.01 mF cm⁻²) and Ni₂P (2.86 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S16 shows the C_dl of NiCoP (4.25 mF cm⁻²) is larger than the Co_xP (3.01 mF cm⁻²) and Ni_2P (2.86 mF cm⁻²).
